newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas opens lower, then edges up.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas opens lower, then edges up.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures opened down slightly Thursday, then edged higher on technical buying at support and talk of steady-to-firmer physical prices, industry sources said.
At 1155 EDT, June was up 2.9 cents at $2.235 per million British thermal units after dipping early to $2.185. July was 2.3 cents higher at $2.27. Most others also were up.

"We've got mild weather and a holiday weekend ahead, and the market still can't come off. There's obviously some underpinning demand out there that I don't understand, and I've given up on the downside," said one Texas-based trader.

Despite bearish weather forecasts next week, traders said steady injection demand has provided good support for the market this month and some said the bears may be running out of time, with better air conditioning demand, particularly in Texas and the South, expected soon.
Normal to slightly below-normal temperatures are expected for most of the nation into early next week. Western states and parts of the Southeast were forecast above-normal for the period.

Technical traders said the market was still range-bound, with June support and resistance still at $2.15 and $2.30, respectively. Major buying was likely at the $2.05 double bottom, with good selling expected at the $2.43 contract high.

In the cash Thursday, Gulf Coast swing prices were steady to up slightly in the high-teens. Midcon pipes were little changed in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also held relatively steady in the mid-$2.40s.
Transco said 400 mmcfd of gas capacity on its Texas mainline, still cut this week due to planned maintenance, should be fully restored by tomorrow. The line has a capacity of 600 mmcfd.

Planned work on Mobil's Mary Ann gas processing plant in Coden, Ala., has cut the plant's total processing capacity of 380-390 mmcfd. About 120 mmcfd should be back by early next week, with the balance due back in three weeks.
NYMEX said 16,140 contracts traded at 1125 EDT. Hub open interest on May 21 rose 597 contracts to 208,817.

On KCBT, June gained one cent to $2.08, while deferreds were steady to two cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 1.9 cents to 15.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT open interest on May 21 rose 62 lots to 2,809.
